title: COMET: Fine-grained Computation-communication Overlapping for Mixture-of-Experts
problem: In distributed MoE models, inter-device all-to-all communication occupies up to 47% of total execution time. Existing coarse-grained overlapping schemes impair computational efficiency and provide sub-optimal latency concealment.
motivation: Sparse MoE models with expert parallelism require all-to-all token routing across GPUs. Naive pipelining partitions expert computation into chunks, but granularity mismatches between token-level communication and tile-level GEMM computation cause inefficiency. Dynamic token routing creates varying workloads that prevent deterministic kernel scheduling.
method: COMET introduces two mechanisms: (1) Shared Tensor Based Dependency Resolving: analyzes the shared buffers between producer (communication) and consumer (computation) operations, decomposes shared tensors along independent dimensions (M-axis for layer0 GEMM, N-axis for layer1 top-K reduction), and reschedules computation tiles to begin as early as possible using local data first. (2) Adaptive Workload Assignment: thread-block specialization isolates communication and computation in separate SM groups within a fused kernel, with adaptive thread-block allocation profiled per input shape and parallelism strategy.
key_novelty: Fine-grained fused GPU kernels that resolve the granularity mismatch between token-level communication and tile-level GEMM computation through shared tensor decomposition and rescheduling, combined with adaptive SM allocation that dynamically balances communication vs. compute SMs at runtime.
contributions: Shared tensor based dependency resolving enabling fine-grained communication-computation overlap
Tensor decomposition and rescheduling along M-axis (layer0) and N-axis (layer1)
Thread-block specialization isolating comm/compute in fused kernels
Adaptive thread-block assignment profiled per (input-shape, parallelism) configuration
NVSHMEM integration for fine-grained GPU-initiated communication
1.96x single MoE layer speedup, 1.71x end-to-end speedup
Deployed in production on 10,000+ GPU clusters saving millions of GPU hours
limitations: Requires pre-profiling per (shape, parallelism) configuration to select optimal thread-block split; NVSHMEM memory overhead (small but non-zero); primarily validated on H800/L20; L20 (PCIe) gains smaller (1.19-1.46x) than H800 (NVLink).
